examples.ko: 그 가게는 올해 커피 브랜드에 가맹했어요.
examples.en: That shop joined a coffee brand this year.
If you join the association, you get several benefits.

examples.ko: 이 카드는 가맹한 가게에서만 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: This card can only be used at member stores.

examples.ko: 우리 식당도 배달 앱에 가맹하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Our restaurant also decided to join the delivery app.
To join, you first have to submit an application.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 국제기구에 가맹한 지 오래됐어요.
examples.en: That country joined the international organization long ago.

explain: 단체, 협회, 프랜차이즈 본사에 공식으로 들어가는 것을 말해요. 일반 모임이나 동아리에 들어갈 때는 '가입하다'를 써요. '가맹점'(프랜차이즈 가게)이라는 말로 더 자주 만나요.
explain_en: It means formally joining an organization, association or franchise headquarters. For ordinary clubs, use '가입하다'. You will more often meet it in the word '가맹점' (franchise store).

dis.h: business joining an association or franchise

p.n: 가맹 is for businesses or groups joining an alliance; 가입 is general membership.

examples.ko: 다행히 사고가 경미해서 다친 사람은 없어요.
examples.en: Luckily the accident was minor, so nobody was hurt.
The damage from this earthquake is relatively slight.

examples.ko: 접촉 사고라서 차 손상이 아주 경미해요.
examples.en: It was just a fender bender, so the damage to the car is very minor.

examples.ko: 부상이 경미하면 병원에 안 가도 될까요?
examples.en: If the injury is minor, is it okay not to go to the hospital?

examples.ko: 경미하게 다쳐서 하루만 쉬고 바로 출근했어요.
examples.en: I was only slightly hurt, so I rested one day and went straight back to work.

examples.ko: 증상이 경미했지만 의사 선생님은 푹 쉬라고 했어요.
examples.en: The symptoms were mild, but the doctor told me to rest well.

explain: '가벼운'과 달리 사고, 부상, 피해, 위반처럼 좋지 않은 일이 크지 않을 때 써요. 뉴스에서 '경미한 부상'처럼 나오고, 반대는 '심각하다'예요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '가벼운' (light), it is used when something bad such as an accident, injury, damage or violation is not serious. You see it in news phrases like '경미한 부상' (minor injury), and its opposite is '심각하다' (serious).

examples.ko: 이 약속은 법적으로 구속력을 갖지 못해요.
examples.en: This promise has no legally binding force.

examples.ko: 양해각서는 법적 구속력이 약해서 나중에 정식 계약을 따로 써요.
examples.en: A memorandum of understanding has weak legal force, so a formal contract is written separately later.
A recommendation isn't binding, but it's hard to ignore.

examples.ko: 구속력 있는 합의라서 함부로 어길 수 없어요.
examples.en: It's a binding agreement, so you can't break it carelessly.

examples.ko: 구속력도 없는 말에 너무 의지하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't rely too much on words that aren't even binding.

examples.ko: 이 규정은 구속력에 한계가 있어서 안 지키는 사람도 많아요.
examples.en: This rule has limits to its enforceability, so many people don't follow it.

explain: 법, 계약, 약속이 사람을 지키게 만드는 힘을 말해요. '법적 구속력이 있다/없다', '구속력을 갖다'처럼 자주 써요. '구속'은 체포라는 뜻으로도 쓰이지만 '구속력'은 그런 뜻이 아니에요.
explain_en: It is the power of a law, contract, or promise to make people comply. Common patterns are '법적 구속력이 있다/없다' and '구속력을 갖다'. '구속' can also mean arrest, but '구속력' does not carry that meaning.

en: belong to; revert to; be vested in

examples.en: Ownership of this land belongs to the state.
The invention made at work became the property of the company.

examples.ko: 계약이 끝나면 건물이 주인에게 귀속된다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the building goes to the owner when the contract ends.
All the profit will go to the school.
Check where the copyright belongs.
Property that has been vested is used for the public.

explain: 재산·권리·책임이 어느 한쪽의 것이 될 때 쓰는 법률·계약 쪽 말이에요. 보통 '~에 귀속되다'로 쓰고, 일상에서 물건이 누구 것이 되는 건 '~의 것이 되다'라고 해요. 서류와 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a legal and contract word for when property, rights or responsibility become one party's. It usually appears as '~에 귀속되다'. In daily life, for an object becoming someone's, people say '~의 것이 되다'.

en: be stipulated; be defined (by rules or law)

examples.en: This is set down by law.

examples.ko: 회사 규칙에 휴가 일수가 규정되어 있어요.
examples.en: The number of vacation days is specified in the company rules.
The school set a separate rule for uniforms.
Please do it as stipulated in the contract.
How are the fines stipulated?
If something is not specified, ask the teacher.

explain: 법, 계약서, 규칙에 적혀 있다는 말이라 보통 문서나 뉴스에서 봐요. 일상 대화에서는 '정해져 있다'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means something is written down in a law, contract or rule, so you mostly see it in documents and the news. In everyday talk, '정해져 있다' is more common.

examples.en: This company received exclusive sales rights for five years.

examples.ko: 독점권을 가진 업체가 가격을 마음대로 정해요.
examples.en: The company with exclusive rights sets prices as it likes.

examples.ko: 이 경기의 중계 독점권은 한 방송사에 있어요.
examples.en: One broadcaster holds the exclusive rights to air this game.

examples.ko: 독점권 계약이 끝나면 다른 회사도 팔 수 있어요.
examples.en: Once the exclusivity contract ends, other companies can sell it too.

examples.ko: 그 작가의 번역 독점권 때문에 협상 중이에요.
examples.en: They are negotiating over the exclusive translation rights to that author's work.

examples.ko: 독점권이 없어서 누구나 이 제품을 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: There are no exclusive rights, so anyone can make this product.

explain: 계약이나 특허로 한 사람이나 한 회사만 가질 수 있는 권리를 말해요. '독점 판매권', '독점 중계권'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여서도 많이 써요. 계약·방송·특허 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a right that only one person or company can hold, through a contract or patent. It is often extended as '독점 판매권' or '독점 중계권'. You'll hear it in talk about contracts, broadcasting and patents.

examples.ko: 집 주인이 누구인지는 등기부등본에서 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can check who owns a house in the registry copy.

examples.ko: 집을 계약하기 전에 등기부를 꼭 확인하세요.
examples.en: Be sure to check the property register before signing a housing contract.

examples.ko: 등기부에 이름이 올라 있어야 진짜 집주인이에요.
examples.en: Only someone whose name is on the register is the real owner.

examples.ko: 발급받은 등기부 내용이 계약서와 달라서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that the register I got differed from the contract.

examples.ko: 등기부의 소유자와 계약하는 사람이 같은지 봤어요.
examples.en: I checked whether the owner on the register is the same person signing the contract.

examples.ko: 땅 등기부에는 주인이 바뀐 기록이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The land register keeps a record of when the owner changed.

explain: 집이나 땅을 사고팔 때 자주 듣는 말이에요. 서류로는 '등기부등본'이라는 말을 쓰고, '등본을 떼다'처럼 말하기도 해요. 요즘 공식 서류 이름은 '등기사항전부증명서'예요.
explain_en: You hear it often when buying or selling a house or land. The document is called '등기부등본', and people say things like '등본을 떼다' (to get a copy). The current official name of the document is '등기사항전부증명서'.

examples.en: The CEO will complete his term at the end of this year.
After serving out his term, a new CEO came in.
He completed his service period and was discharged.
A man who completed his sentence was released today.
Once the contract period ends, the rate changes.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 전속 계약을 만료하고 새 회사로 옮겼어요.
examples.en: The singer finished his exclusive contract and moved to a new company.

explain: '임기를 만료하다', '형기를 만료하다'처럼 주로 공문서와 뉴스에서 써요. 일상에서는 '만료되다'나 '끝나다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 목적어를 받는 타동사로 쓰면 '기간을 다 채우고 끝내다'라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It appears mostly in official documents and news, as in 임기를 만료하다 and 형기를 만료하다. In daily speech 만료되다 or 끝나다 is more natural. Used transitively, it carries a sense of finishing out the full period.

examples.ko: 이 집은 아버지 명의로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This house is registered in my father's name.

examples.ko: 남의 명의를 빌려서 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not borrow and use someone else's name.
The company name is written on the contract.

examples.ko: 명의 변경은 은행에서 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can change the name on the account at the bank.
I bought the car in my older brother's name.
Whose name is this card under, anyway?

explain: 집, 차, 통장, 휴대폰 같은 계약에서 법적으로 이름이 올라 있는 사람을 말할 때 '누구 명의'라고 해요. 같은 소리로 '이름난 훌륭한 의사'라는 다른 단어(명의)도 있으니 문장을 보고 구분해요.
explain_en: Used in contracts for houses, cars, bank accounts and phones to say whose name is legally on it, as in 누구 명의. There is another word with the same sound, 명의, meaning a famous skilled doctor, so tell them apart by context.

examples.en: This shop's quality is guaranteed.
The safety of personal information must be guaranteed.
There's no method that guarantees you'll pass.
Workers' right to rest is guaranteed.

examples.ko: 성공이 보장되지 않아도 해 볼 거예요.
examples.en: Even if success isn't guaranteed, I'll try.
I want to live in a country where freedom is guaranteed.

explain: 품질, 안전, 권리, 결과 같은 것이 틀림없이 지켜진다는 뜻이에요. 사람이 약속하는 '보장하다'와 짝이고, '보장되다'는 그 약속이 이미 지켜지는 상태예요. 광고에서 '품질 보장'이라는 명사 형태로도 많이 봐요.
explain_en: It means things like quality, safety, rights, or results are surely upheld. It pairs with 보장하다, where a person promises, and 보장되다 is the state of that promise being kept. In ads you often see the noun form, like 품질 보장.

en: use as a pretext; do under the guise of

examples.ko: 그는 친구 사이를 빙자해서 돈을 빌려 갔어요.
examples.en: He used their friendship as a pretext to borrow money.
There are too many ads that use health as a pretext.
Using studying as a cover, I secretly just played games.

examples.ko: 사랑을 빙자해 상대를 마음대로 하려는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people use love as an excuse to control their partner.

examples.ko: 친절을 빙자하여 개인 정보를 묻는 전화가 많아졌어요.
examples.en: There are more calls that pretend to be kind in order to ask for personal information.
I used work as a cover story, got found out and was scolded.

explain: 어떤 것을 핑계나 구실로 삼아 다른 일을 할 때 써요. 'A를 빙자해서'처럼 말하고, 대개 좋지 않은 속셈이 있다는 느낌이에요. '핑계 대다'보다 딱딱하고, '건강을 빙자한 광고'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 모양으로도 써요.
explain_en: It is used when you take something as a pretext or excuse to do something else, in the pattern 'A를 빙자해서', usually with a bad motive implied. It sounds stiffer than '핑계 대다'. It can also modify a noun, as in '건강을 빙자한 광고'.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 결혼식에서 서로 사랑하겠다고 서약했어요.
examples.en: At the wedding, the two pledged to love each other.
New employees pledge to keep secrets.
The sight of them raising their hands and taking the oath was impressive.

examples.ko: 회원들은 규칙을 지키기로 서약한 뒤 가입했어요.
examples.en: The members joined after pledging to follow the rules.
The president will swear to uphold the constitution.
After taking the pledge, my resolve grew stronger.

explain: '약속하다'보다 훨씬 공식적이고 무거운 말이에요. 사람들 앞이나 문서로 지키겠다고 다짐할 때 써요. 비슷한 '맹세하다'는 마음속 다짐이나 감정이 더 강하고, '서약하다'는 '서약서'를 쓰는 것처럼 공식적인 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is much more formal and weighty than '약속하다'. It is used when committing to something before people or in writing. The similar '맹세하다' is about a heartfelt vow, while '서약하다' has an official feel, like signing a '서약서' (written pledge).

examples.en: The son decided to take over his father's business.
The youngest daughter will take over the shop.

examples.ko: 새 팀장이 전임자의 업무를 그대로 승계해요.
examples.en: The new team leader takes over the predecessor's duties as they are.

examples.ko: 전통을 승계하는 젊은 장인이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of young craftsmen carrying on the tradition is growing.
The prince who succeeded to the throne was still young.

examples.ko: 이 계약은 새 주인이 승계하는 조건이에요.
examples.en: This contract is on the condition that the new owner takes it over.

explain: 지위, 재산, 사업, 계약처럼 앞사람이 하던 것을 그대로 이어받을 때 써요. 가족 회사나 업무 인수인계 같은 딱딱한 상황에서 주로 나와요. 일상에서는 '이어받다'가 더 편해요.
explain_en: It is used when you take over what the previous person held, such as a position, property, business or contract. It mostly appears in formal situations like family companies and work handovers. In daily talk 이어받다 is easier.

examples.en: The court seized that person's house.
The tax office seizes the bank account.

examples.ko: 빚을 못 갚으면 월급도 압류할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you can't repay the debt, they can even seize your salary.

examples.ko: 은행이 차를 압류해서 운전을 못 해요.
examples.en: The bank seized the car, so I can't drive.

examples.ko: 재산을 압류하는 일은 아무나 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Not just anyone can seize property.

examples.ko: 세금을 안 내면 재산을 압류한다고 했어요.
examples.en: They said they would seize your property if you don't pay taxes.

explain: 압류하다는 법원, 세무서, 은행 같은 기관이 하는 일이라 개인이 주어면 어색해요. 개인이 남의 물건을 가져가는 건 '뺏다'나 '가져가다'라고 해요. 당하는 쪽은 '압류당하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: 압류하다 is done by institutions such as a court, tax office, or bank, so it sounds odd with a private person as the subject. When an individual takes someone's things, 뺏다 or 가져가다 is used. The person it happens to is described with 압류당하다.

examples.en: When the contract ends, you have to restore the house to its original state.

examples.ko: 벽에 낸 구멍은 원상회복 비용을 내야 해요.
examples.en: You have to pay restoration costs for the holes in the wall.
It was damaged so badly that restoring it is impossible.
The court ordered the company to restore things to their original state.

examples.ko: 공사 후에 길을 원상회복하는 데 일주일이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a week to restore the road after the construction.

examples.ko: 청소뿐 아니라 원상회복까지 끝내고 열쇠를 돌려줬어요.
examples.en: I finished not just the cleaning but the restoration too, and returned the key.

explain: 집을 빌렸다가 나갈 때, 공사를 한 뒤에 쓰는 말로, 바꾼 것을 원래대로 돌려놓는 것을 말해요. '복구'는 망가진 것을 고치는 것 전반에 쓰고, 원상회복은 '원래 상태'로 돌려놓는다는 점을 강조해요. 뉴스나 계약 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when moving out of a rental or after construction work, meaning to put altered things back as they were. '복구' covers repairing damage in general, while 원상회복 stresses returning to the original state. It shows up often in the news and in contract talk.

examples.en: This action goes against the company rules.

examples.ko: 법에 위배되는 일은 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not do anything that violates the law.
The decision went against the promise, so I protested.

examples.ko: 계약 내용에 위배될 경우 벌금을 내야 해요.
examples.en: If it goes against the contract terms, a fine must be paid.
A ruling came out saying it violates the constitution.

examples.ko: 학교 규정에 위배되지 않는 선에서 해 보세요.
examples.en: Try it within limits that do not go against school regulations.

explain: '어기다'는 사람이 규칙을 직접 어기는 행동이고, '위배되다'는 행동, 결정, 내용이 법, 규칙, 약속에 맞지 않을 때 써요. 그래서 주어는 사람보다 일이나 결정이고, 조사 '에'와 함께 '규칙에 위배되다'로 써요. 계약과 법 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '어기다' is when a person breaks a rule directly. '위배되다' is used when an action, decision or content does not match a law, rule or promise, so the subject is usually a matter or decision rather than a person. It takes '에', as in '규칙에 위배되다', and appears often in contract and legal talk.

examples.ko: 허락 없이 사진을 파는 것은 위법적인 행동이에요.
examples.en: Selling photos without permission is an unlawful act.

examples.ko: 그 회사의 위법적인 관행이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: That company's unlawful practices appeared in the news.
The lawyer argued that this measure is unlawful.

examples.ko: 위법적으로 땅을 사용한 것이 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: Using the land unlawfully became a problem.

examples.ko: 이 계약은 위법적일 가능성이 있어서 다시 검토해야 해요.
examples.en: This contract may be unlawful, so we need to review it again.

examples.ko: 위법적이지 않은지 법률 전문가에게 먼저 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I first asked a legal expert whether it was unlawful.

explain: '불법적'과 비슷하지만 '위법적'은 법규에 어긋났는지 따지는 뉴스나 재판 이야기에 잘 어울려요. 반대말은 '합법적'이에요. '위법적인 N', '위법적이다'로 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '불법적', but '위법적' fits news and court talk where people judge whether something breaks a law or regulation. The opposite is '합법적'. It is used as '위법적인 N' or '위법적이다'.

examples.en: My grandfather wrote a will before he passed away.
The lawyer read the will in front of the family.

examples.ko: 유언장에는 재산을 나누는 방법이 적혀 있었어요.
examples.en: The will described how to divide the property.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 가짜 유언장이 나와서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A fake will appeared in the drama, and I was shocked.
A will must be legally valid.

examples.ko: 그는 서랍 깊숙이 유언장을 숨겨 두었어요.
examples.en: He hid the will deep in a drawer.

explain: 말로 남기면 '유언', 글로 쓴 문서는 '유언장'이에요. '유언장을 쓰다', '유언장을 작성하다', '유언장을 공개하다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스와 드라마에 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A spoken wish is 유언, and the written document is 유언장. You say 유언장을 쓰다, 유언장을 작성하다, 유언장을 공개하다. It appears more in news and dramas than in daily conversation.

examples.en: The constitution protects citizens' property rights.
The landowner claims to hold the property rights.

examples.ko: 아파트 재건축은 주민의 재산권과 관련이 있어요.
examples.en: Apartment reconstruction is related to residents' property rights.
People gathered to protest, calling it an infringement of property rights.
Individual property rights are guaranteed by law.
I consulted a lawyer about the property rights to the land.

explain: 주로 '재산권을 보호하다', '재산권을 침해하다'처럼 법이나 뉴스 이야기에서 나와요. 특허나 저작권 같은 것은 '지식재산권'이라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in talk about law and the news, as in '재산권을 보호하다' or '재산권을 침해하다'. Things like patents and copyrights are separately called '지식재산권' (intellectual property rights).

examples.en: This term is defined by law.
Happiness is defined differently by each person.
Once the problem is defined exactly, it's easier to solve.

examples.ko: 처음에 정의된 뜻과 지금 쓰임이 달라요.
examples.en: The originally defined meaning differs from how it's used now.

examples.ko: 이 단어는 사전에서 어떻게 정의되는지 찾아봤어요.
examples.en: I looked up how this word is defined in the dictionary.
The roles aren't clearly defined, so it's confusing.

explain: 단어, 용어, 문제의 뜻이나 범위가 분명하게 정해질 때 써요. 사람이 하는 '정의하다'와 짝이고 '~로 정의되다'로 어떻게 정해졌는지 말해요. 같은 소리의 '정의'(옳은 것, justice)는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: Used when the meaning or scope of a word, term, or problem is clearly set. It pairs with 정의하다, and you say how with ~로 정의되다. The same-sounding 정의 meaning justice is a different word.

examples.en: The school club decided to expel a member.
The party expelled that lawmaker.

examples.ko: 단체가 규칙을 어긴 사람을 제명할 수 있어요.
examples.en: An organization can expel someone who broke the rules.
The members proposed expelling the president by vote.
Why are you trying to expel me from the group?

examples.ko: 협회는 부정을 저지른 선수를 제명하지 않았어요.
examples.en: The association did not expel the player who cheated.

explain: 'N을/를 제명하다'처럼 단체가 사람을 명단에서 빼 내보낼 때 써요. 일상에서 친구끼리는 '쫓아내다'라고 가볍게 말하기도 하지만, 제명하다는 공식적인 결정이라는 느낌이에요. 반대로 받아 주는 건 '가입시키다'예요.
explain_en: Used as 'N을/를 제명하다' when a group removes a person from its list and sends them out. Friends might casually say '쫓아내다', but 제명하다 sounds like an official decision. The opposite is letting someone in, '가입시키다'.

en: enact; establish (a law, constitution, rule, holiday)

examples.en: The National Assembly enacted a new law.
The city established an Environment Day.
The school will establish a new rule.

examples.ko: 회사가 안전 수칙을 제정한 뒤 사고가 줄었어요.
examples.en: Accidents decreased after the company set safety rules.

examples.ko: 법을 제정하려면 많은 사람의 동의가 필요해요.
examples.en: To enact a law, you need the agreement of many people.

examples.ko: 우리 동아리는 지금 회칙을 제정하는 중이에요.
examples.en: Our club is in the middle of drawing up its bylaws.

explain: 법, 규칙, 기념일처럼 공식적인 것을 새로 만들어 정할 때 써요. '규칙을 만들다'가 일상 말이고, '제정하다'는 문서나 뉴스에 어울려요. 비슷하게 생긴 '개정하다'는 이미 있는 것을 고친다는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It is used when officially creating and fixing something new, such as a law, rule, or commemorative day. '규칙을 만들다' is the everyday phrase, while '제정하다' suits documents and news. The similar-looking '개정하다' differs: it revises something that already exists.

en: be concluded; be signed (of a contract)

examples.en: A contract was concluded between the two companies.
Once the agreement is signed, trade gets easier.
I'll send you the contract that was signed yesterday.

examples.ko: 조약이 체결되기 전에 회의를 세 번 했어요.
examples.en: They held three meetings before the treaty was concluded.
The contract will be signed next week.

examples.ko: 합의는 했지만 아직 계약이 체결되지 않았어요.
examples.en: We agreed, but the contract hasn't been signed yet.

explain: 계약·협정·조약처럼 문서로 남기는 약속에 써요. 사람이 주어가 아니라 계약이 주어라서 '계약이 체결되다'로 말하고, 하는 쪽을 말할 때는 '계약을 체결하다'를 써요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '계약하다', '사인하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Used for formal commitments put on paper: contracts, agreements, treaties. The contract is the subject ('계약이 체결되다'); when you name the people acting, use '계약을 체결하다'. In everyday talk Koreans usually say '계약하다' or '사인하다'.

examples.ko: 아이의 휴대폰 사용에 대한 통제권은 부모에게 있어요.
examples.en: Parents have control over their child's phone use.

examples.ko: 이 일은 제 통제권 밖이라서 어쩔 수 없어요.
examples.en: This is outside my control, so there's nothing I can do.

examples.ko: 회사가 모든 정보의 통제권을 갖고 있어요.
examples.en: The company holds control over all the information.

examples.ko: 저는 제 삶의 통제권을 되찾고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to take back control of my life.
It's dangerous when a driver loses control of the car.
I don't know who has taken control of the situation.

explain: '통제권을 갖다/잃다/되찾다/넘기다'처럼 동사와 함께 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '내 마음대로 할 수 없는 일이에요'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is often paired with verbs like '갖다', '잃다', '되찾다' and '넘기다'. In casual talk people often rephrase it, for example '내 마음대로 할 수 없는 일이에요' (It's not something I can decide).

en: be annulled; be broken off (a contract, promise); be destroyed (documents)

examples.en: The contract was suddenly annulled and everyone was shocked.
When a promise is broken, people lose trust in each other.

examples.ko: 파기된 계약서는 다시 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.en: A contract that has been annulled can't be used again.

examples.ko: 합의가 파기될 때는 이유를 분명히 알려야 해요.
examples.en: When an agreement is broken off, you must state the reason clearly.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 협약이 파기되어서 거래가 끊겼어요.
examples.en: The two companies' agreement was annulled, so their dealings stopped.
A rumor spread that the engagement had been called off.

explain: 계약, 약속, 조약처럼 서로 지키기로 한 것이 깨질 때 써요. '취소되다'는 행사나 예약처럼 가볍게 없어질 때 써요. 하는 쪽은 '파기하다'이고, 비밀 서류를 없앨 때도 '파기하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it when something both sides agreed to keep, such as a contract, promise or treaty, gets broken. 취소되다 is for lighter things like events or reservations being cancelled. The active form is 파기하다, which is also used for destroying secret documents.

examples.ko: 계약을 파기하면 돈을 물어 줘야 해요.
examples.en: If you cancel the contract, you have to pay damages.
Please destroy the documents that aren't important.
The company decided to delete the personal data.
My friend got very angry because I broke our promise.
The court overturned the earlier ruling.
We destroyed the old records according to the rules.

explain: 일상에서는 '약속을 깨다'라고 하고, '계약을 파기하다'는 공식적인 말투예요. 개인 정보나 서류를 완전히 없앨 때도 써요. 법원에서는 앞선 판결을 취소할 때 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk you say '약속을 깨다' (break a promise); '계약을 파기하다' (cancel a contract) is the formal version. It is also used for fully destroying personal data or documents, and for a court overturning an earlier ruling.

examples.ko: 그 사업의 합법성을 두고 논란이 커지고 있어요.
examples.en: Controversy is growing over the legality of that business.

examples.ko: 계약하기 전에 이 업체의 합법성을 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Check this company's legitimacy before signing a contract.
The court recognized the legality of the protest.

examples.ko: 합법성만 따지지 말고 도덕적으로도 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't just consider legality, think about it morally too.

examples.ko: 새 서비스의 합법성이 아직 분명하지 않아요.
examples.en: The legality of the new service is still unclear.
I asked a lawyer about the legality of this method.

explain: '합법'은 법에 맞는 것이고 '합법성'은 그 정도나 성질을 말해요. '합법성을 따지다', '합법성을 인정하다', '합법성 논란'처럼 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 반대말은 '불법성'이에요.
explain_en: '합법' means being within the law, and '합법성' refers to that quality or degree. It often appears in news as '합법성을 따지다' (question the legality), '합법성을 인정하다' (recognize the legality) or '합법성 논란' (legality controversy). The opposite is '불법성'.

examples.en: Photography is allowed here.
Pets aren't allowed in the dorm.
Dictionary use was allowed during the exam.

examples.ko: 허용된 시간 안에 문제를 풀어야 해요.
examples.en: You must solve the problems within the allowed time.

examples.ko: 조금 늦는 건 허용되지만 너무 늦으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Being a little late is tolerated, but not too late.

examples.ko: 이 정도 실수는 허용될 것 같아요.
examples.en: A mistake this small seems acceptable.

explain: 규칙이나 상황이 그렇게 하는 것을 막지 않을 때 써요. '허가되다'가 신청해서 받는 승인이라면, '허용되다'는 이미 정해진 규칙 안에서 가능하다는 느낌이에요. 표지판에는 '금지'의 반대로 '허용'이라고 써요.
explain_en: Used when the rules or situation don't forbid something. Where '허가되다' implies applying and receiving approval, '허용되다' means it is possible within established rules. On signs, it is the opposite of '금지'.

dis.h: allowed or tolerated within the rules

p.n: 허가 suggests permission must be asked for; 허용 is a general allowance.
